easy.def: A wild pig.
examples: A boar ran through the woods.
The boar has tusks.
We saw a wild boar.

more.def: A wild pig with tusks, or a male pig on a farm.
examples: A wild boar rooted for acorns in the forest.
The boar has two long tusks that curve upward.
The farmer kept one boar and many sows on the farm.

easy.def: A flat piece of wood.
examples: The bridge is made of boards.
Dad cut a board.
A board fell off the fence.

more.def: A long, flat piece of wood.
examples: He nailed a board over the hole in the fence.
The old bridge had a loose board.
Dad sawed the board in half.

easy.def: A flat surface for games or writing.
examples: The teacher writes on the board.
We play on a game board.
The chess board is set up.

more.def: A flat surface used for a game or for writing on.
examples: The teacher wrote the words on the board.
We set up the chess board.
The checkers are on the board.

easy.def: To get on a train, plane or ship.
examples: We board the plane.
Please board the bus.
They boarded the ship.

more.def: To get on a train, plane, bus or ship.
examples: Passengers boarded the plane in a line.
We board the bus at eight.
Please board the train now.

easy.def: Getting on a plane, bus or ship.
examples: Boarding begins at noon.
We waited for boarding.
The boarding line was long.

more.def: The act of getting on a plane, train or ship.
examples: Boarding begins at gate five.
The families waited for boarding to start.
A boarding pass lets you get on the plane.

easy.def: A path made of wood boards by the sea.
examples: We walked on the boardwalk.
The boardwalk is by the beach.
A boardwalk has shops.

more.def: A wide walkway made of wooden boards, usually next to a beach.
examples: We strolled along the boardwalk and ate ice cream.
The boardwalk has shops, games and rides beside the sea.
He rode his bike along the boardwalk.

easy.def: To brag about something you did.
examples: Do not boast.
He boasted about his score.
She boasts about her pet.

more.def: To talk about yourself or what you own in a proud way that makes others feel bad.
examples: He boasted about his high score until his friends felt bored.
She boasts about her new bike.
Do not boast about winning; just be happy.

easy.def: A small vehicle that floats on water.
examples: We rode in a boat.
The boat sailed away.
Fish swim near the boat.

more.def: A small vehicle that travels on water.
examples: We paddled the boat across the lake.
A fishing boat left the harbor at dawn.
The sailboat leaned in the wind.

easy.def: Having to do with the body.
examples: Hunger is a bodily need.
Bodily strength.
A bodily feeling.

more.def: Having to do with the human body.
examples: Food and sleep are bodily needs that everyone has.
Exercise improves your bodily strength.
Hunger is a bodily feeling that tells you to eat.

easy.def: All of a person or animal, from head to foot.
examples: My body is strong.
Wash your body.
A bird has a small body.

more.def: The whole physical form of a person or animal, including the head, arms, and legs.
examples: Exercise helps keep your body healthy.
The giraffe has a long neck and a small body.
She wrapped a towel around her body after swimming.

easy.def: A person who protects someone important.
examples: The bodyguard stood by the door.
The singer has a bodyguard.
The bodyguard watched the crowd.

more.def: A person whose job is to protect someone who may be in danger.
examples: The bodyguard stood beside the president.
The singer arrived with a bodyguard.
The bodyguard watched the crowd closely.

easy.def: An area of wet, soft ground.
examples: The bog was muddy.
Frogs live in the bog.
We walked around the bog.

more.def: An area of wet, soft, spongy ground where mosses and other plants grow.
examples: Frogs and dragonflies live in the wet bog.
Our boots sank into the soft ground of the bog.
Cranberries grow in a bog.

easy.def: Fake and not real.
examples: The coin was bogus.
He gave a bogus excuse.
It was a bogus ticket.

more.def: Not real or true, but made to look like it is.
examples: The bogus coin was made of plastic, not gold.
His bogus excuse about a lost shoe did not fool the teacher.
The ticket turned out to be bogus, so we could not go in.

easy.def: To heat water until it bubbles.
examples: I boil water.
The water is boiling.
Boil the eggs.

more.def: To heat a liquid until it bubbles and gives off steam.
examples: Mom boiled the water for tea.
Boil the potatoes until they are soft.
The water boils at a high heat.

easy.def: A big tank that heats water for a building.
examples: The boiler is in the basement.
Our boiler heats the house.
The boiler made a noise.

more.def: A large metal tank in which water is heated to warm a building or to make steam.
examples: The boiler in the basement heats the water for the whole school.
The old steam engine burned coal to heat its boiler.
A repairman came to fix the broken boiler on the coldest day of winter.

easy.def: Brave and not shy.
examples: The bold girl spoke up.
He is a bold boy.
The bold knight rode in.

more.def: Not afraid, or very strong and clear.
examples: The bold girl spoke up in front of everyone.
He made a bold move in the game.
The poster used bold letters.

easy.def: In a brave way.
examples: He boldly jumped in.
She boldly asked a question.
The knight boldly stepped forward.

more.def: In a brave, confident way.
examples: He boldly jumped into the cold lake.
She boldly asked the teacher a hard question.
The knight boldly stepped forward to face the dragon.

easy.def: A metal pin with a screw thread.
examples: The bolt holds the wheel.
He tightened the bolt.
The bolt is rusty.

more.def: A strong metal pin with a screw on it, used to hold things together.
examples: Dad tightened the bolt on the swing.
A rusty bolt held the gate.
The mechanic replaced a loose bolt.

easy.def: A flash of lightning.
examples: A bolt of lightning struck.
I saw a bolt in the sky.
The bolt lit the night.

more.def: A sudden bright flash of lightning.
examples: A bolt of lightning lit up the sky.
The bolt struck a tree.
We counted after the bolt to hear the thunder.

easy.def: A thing that blows up and can hurt people.
examples: A bomb is very dangerous.
The soldiers in the story dropped a bomb.
The bomb squad checked the box.

more.def: A weapon or device that can explode and cause damage.
examples: The old bomb from the war was removed safely.
Experts cleared the field of the bomb.
In the film, the hero stopped the bomb.

easy.def: A lot of something good.
examples: It was a bonanza of fruit.
A bonanza of toys.
The garden was a bonanza.

more.def: A source of a great amount of something good, such as money or a large supply of something.
examples: The apple tree was a bonanza that gave us fruit all fall.
The miners hoped to find a gold bonanza.
The yard sale was a bonanza of bargains.

easy.def: One of the hard white parts inside your body.
examples: I broke a bone.
Dogs chew bones.
Bones hold you up.

more.def: One of the hard, white parts that make up the skeleton inside the body.
examples: The dog buried a bone in the yard.
Your bones hold your body up.
She learned the names of the bones in her hand.

easy.def: A big fire outside.
examples: We sat by the bonfire.
The bonfire was warm.
They lit a bonfire.

more.def: A large fire that is built outdoors, often for a celebration or to keep people warm.
examples: We roasted marshmallows around the bonfire on the beach.
The bonfire crackled and sent sparks into the night sky.
The town lit a bonfire to celebrate the harvest.

easy.def: A hat that ties under the chin.
examples: The baby wore a bonnet.
A pink bonnet.
She tied her bonnet.

more.def: A hat that is tied under the chin, worn by babies or by women in the past.
examples: The baby wore a white bonnet tied with a ribbon.
The pioneer girl wore a bonnet to keep the sun off her face.
Her Easter bonnet had flowers on it.

easy.def: An extra thing you get.
examples: We got a bonus.
The bonus was a free toy.
Dad got a bonus at work.

more.def: Something extra that you get in addition to what you expected.
examples: We got a bonus point for good teamwork.
The free toy was a bonus.
Finding a coin on the path was a nice bonus.

easy.def: A word you say to scare someone as a joke.
examples: I jumped out and said, "Boo!"
Boo! Did I scare you?
She hid and shouted boo.

more.def: A word you shout to make someone jump, as a joke, or to show you do not like something.
examples: I jumped out from behind the door and shouted, "Boo!"
The ghost in the play said boo to the children.
The kids said boo at the sleepy dog.

easy.def: To dance to lively music.
examples: We boogie to the song.
The kids boogied.
Let's boogie!

more.def: To dance in a fun, lively way.
examples: We boogied to the song at the party.
The kids boogied around the room.
Let's boogie to the music.

easy.def: Pages with words or pictures that you read.
examples: I read a book.
She has a new book.
This book is funny.

more.def: A set of pages with words or pictures that are joined together in a cover.
examples: I borrowed a book about space from the library.
My favorite book has a green cover and a hundred pages.
This book has a story about a dragon.

easy.def: A shop that sells books.
examples: We went to the bookstore.
The bookstore has many books.
I bought a book at the bookstore.

more.def: A store where books are sold.
examples: We visited the bookstore and picked out a new adventure story.
The bookstore on the corner has a cozy reading nook for kids.
The author signed copies of her book at the bookstore.

easy.def: A deep, loud sound.
examples: I heard a boom.
The thunder gave a boom.
A boom shook the house.

more.def: A very loud, deep sound like thunder or a big drum.
examples: A boom of thunder made the dog hide.
The drum made a deep boom.
We heard the boom of fireworks.

easy.def: To make a deep, loud sound.
examples: The thunder boomed.
The drum booms.
His voice boomed.

more.def: To make a deep, loud sound that echoes.
examples: Thunder boomed over the hills.
The big drum boomed in the parade.
The teacher's voice boomed across the gym.

easy.def: To lift or help.
examples: I boost my friend up.
The snack boosted my energy.
A good sleep boosts your mood.

more.def: To lift or push up something, or to make it stronger.
examples: I boosted my friend up the wall.
A snack boosted my energy.
Praise boosted her confidence.

easy.def: A thing that makes something stronger or higher.
examples: The rocket has a booster.
A seat booster helped her see.
The booster gave the team energy.

more.def: Something that adds to the power or effect of something else, such as a part of a rocket or a medicine.
examples: The rocket has a booster at the bottom.
A booster seat helps small children see out the car window.
I got a booster shot at the doctor.

easy.def: A strong shoe that covers your ankle.
examples: I wear rain boots.
My boot has mud on it.
The boot is warm.

more.def: A strong shoe that covers the foot and part of the leg.
examples: I wear rain boots when it pours.
He put on his hiking boots for the trail.
Mud stuck to my boots.

easy.def: A small closed place for one job or a small stand.
examples: Buy a ticket at the booth.
The booth sells popcorn.
The photo booth is fun.

more.def: A small area or stand that is partly closed in, used for selling things or for privacy.
examples: We bought tickets at the ticket booth.
Our class ran a booth at the school fair.
A phone booth has glass walls and a door.

easy.def: The edge of something, or the line between two countries.
examples: The picture has a blue border.
The river is the border.
We crossed the border.

more.def: The edge of something, or the line that separates two places or countries.
examples: The picture has a red border around it.
The river forms the border between the two countries.
We showed our passports when we crossed the border.

easy.def: Right on the edge between two things.
examples: A borderline case.
The score was borderline.
It was borderline.

more.def: Right on the line between two things, so that it is hard to say which one it belongs to.
examples: Her test score was borderline, just between a pass and a fail.
It was a borderline call, and the umpire had to think.
The weather was borderline, not quite warm enough for a swim.

easy.def: To make someone tired of something.
examples: The long story bored me.
Homework bores him.
The speech bored the class.

more.def: To make someone feel tired and not interested.
examples: The long talk bored the whole class.
Waiting in line can bore anyone.
The same game every day bores me.

easy.def: To make a hole.
examples: The worm bores into the apple.
The drill bored a hole.
Workers bored a tunnel.

more.def: To make a hole by cutting or turning a tool through something.
examples: The beetle bores into the tree.
Workers bored a tunnel through the mountain.
The drill bored a hole in the wood.

easy.def: Tired of something that is not interesting.
examples: I am bored.
He was bored in the car.
The kids were bored.

more.def: Feeling tired and restless because you have nothing interesting to do.
examples: I was bored on the long car ride.
The bored cat stared out the window.
She felt bored until her friend arrived.

easy.def: The feeling of having nothing fun to do.
examples: Boredom made me yawn.
I felt boredom.
Boredom is no fun.

more.def: The tired feeling that you get when you have nothing interesting to do.
examples: On the long car ride, boredom set in, so we played word games.
The rainy day filled us with boredom until Mom brought out the board games.
He drew pictures to beat the boredom.

easy.def: Not interesting.
examples: The movie was boring.
This is a boring game.
Waiting is boring.

more.def: Dull and not interesting, so that you feel tired of it.
examples: The long, boring speech made me sleepy.
Doing the same chore every day can be boring.
The trip was boring until we saw a deer.

easy.def: To start life.
examples: A baby was born today.
I was born in May.
The calf was born in spring.

more.def: To be brought into the world at birth.
examples: My little sister was born in the spring.
The puppies were born in the barn.
Where were you born?

easy.def: To use something that is not yours and then give it back.
examples: Can I borrow your red crayon?
I borrow books from my friend.
May I borrow your pencil?

more.def: To take and use something that belongs to someone else, planning to return it.
examples: She borrowed three books from the library and returned them on Friday.
He borrowed his dad's umbrella because it was raining.
You can borrow a board game from the classroom shelf.

easy.def: The person in charge at work.
examples: Mom's boss is kind.
The boss gave us jobs.
Who is the boss here?

more.def: A person who is in charge of other workers.
examples: The boss thanked the workers for finishing early.
My dad asked his boss for a day off.
The bakery's boss starts work before dawn.

easy.def: Always telling others what to do.
examples: She is bossy.
Don't be bossy.
A bossy kid.

more.def: Fond of telling other people what to do in a rude or too forceful way.
examples: My older sister is bossy and tells me where to sit.
Don't be bossy; let everyone have a turn to choose.
The bossy parrot squawked orders at everyone.

easy.def: The two of them.
examples: I like both.
Both are good.
Hold it with both hands.

more.def: The one and the other of two people or things.
examples: Both of my brothers play the guitar.
I tried the red and the blue shirts, and I like both.
Both teams ran onto the field at the same time.

easy.def: To make someone upset by interrupting.
examples: Do not bother the baby.
The noise bothers me.
Flies bother the horse.

more.def: To annoy someone or interrupt them, or to cause worry.
examples: The loud music bothered the neighbors.
Please do not bother me while I read.
Does the cold bother you?

easy.def: A container for drinks with a narrow top.
examples: A bottle of milk.
Water in a bottle.
The baby drinks from a bottle.

more.def: A container, usually of glass or plastic, with a narrow neck for holding liquids.
examples: She filled the bottle with water.
He put a message in a bottle.
The baby drinks milk from a bottle.

easy.def: The lowest part of something.
examples: The toy is at the bottom of the box.
Sink to the bottom.
Sign your name at the bottom.

more.def: The lowest part of something, farthest from the top.
examples: A coin lay at the bottom of the pool.
The answer is at the bottom of the page.
We waited at the bottom of the stairs.

easy.def: Lowest.
examples: The bottom shelf is full of toys.
Look at the bottom drawer.
He is in the bottom bunk.

more.def: Placed at the lowest point.
examples: Put the heavy books on the bottom shelf.
The bottom bunk is easier for little kids.
The cat sleeps in the bottom drawer.

easy.def: To spring back after hitting something.
examples: The ball will bounce.
I bounce the ball.
The ball bounced off the wall.

more.def: To spring back quickly after hitting something.
examples: The ball bounced twice before she caught it.
She bounced the ball on the floor.
The kids bounced on the trampoline.

easy.def: A spring back after hitting something.
examples: The ball took a high bounce.
I heard a bounce.
The bounce was high.

more.def: The act of springing back after hitting something.
examples: The bounce of the basketball echoed through the gym.
The bounce of the rubber ball surprised us.
A high bounce sent it over the fence.

easy.def: Full of bounce.
examples: A bouncy ball.
The bed is bouncy.
The puppy is bouncy.

more.def: Full of bounce, so that it springs back or moves in a lively way.
examples: A bouncy ball sprang high off the pavement.
The bouncy castle was a hit at the party.
The puppy was so bouncy that it leaped all around the yard.

easy.def: Sure to happen.
examples: She is bound to win.
It is bound to rain.
The ice is bound to melt.

more.def: Certain or sure to do something.
examples: The team is bound to win after all that practice.
It is bound to rain with those dark clouds.
He is bound to be late again.

easy.def: To jump with long steps.
examples: The deer bounded across the field.
The puppy bounded up the stairs.
She bounded down the hall.

more.def: To leap or run with long, springy steps.
examples: The deer bounded across the meadow.
The puppy bounded up the steps to greet us.
She bounded out of bed on the first day of vacation.

easy.def: A line that shows where a place ends.
examples: The fence is the boundary of our yard.
The white line is the boundary of the field.
A wall marks the boundary of the farm.

more.def: A line or edge that marks where one area ends and another begins.
examples: The river forms the boundary between the two countries.
The ball rolled past the boundary, so play stopped.
Mountains form a natural boundary between the two valleys.

easy.def: A reward for catching something.
examples: A bounty was offered.
The bounty was one hundred dollars.
They offered a bounty.

more.def: A reward that is offered for finding or catching something or someone.
examples: A bounty was offered for the lost dog.
The town offered a bounty for the rats.
A large bounty was offered for the missing treasure.

easy.def: A large amount of something good.
examples: The garden gave a bounty of tomatoes.
The farm's bounty was great.
A bounty of fruit.

more.def: A rich supply of something good.
examples: The garden gave us a bounty of tomatoes.
The harvest was a bounty.
The orchard offered a bounty of apples.

easy.def: A bunch of flowers.
examples: She got a bouquet.
The bouquet is pretty.
I picked a bouquet.

more.def: A bunch of flowers that are tied together to be given or carried.
examples: She carried a bouquet of roses down the aisle.
I picked a bouquet of wild flowers for my mom.
A bouquet of tulips sat on the kitchen table.

easy.def: To bend forward to show thanks or respect.
examples: The actors bow.
I bowed to the teacher.
The dancers bowed.

more.def: To bend your body forward at the waist to show respect or to thank an audience.
examples: The actors bowed at the end of the play.
The knights bowed to the queen.
She bowed her head in thanks.

easy.def: A ribbon tied in a pretty way.
examples: She tied a bow in her hair.
The gift has a red bow.
The ribbon makes a bow.

more.def: A knot made with loops, used to tie ribbons and shoelaces.
examples: He tied his shoes with a neat bow.
A big red bow decorated the gift.
She wore a bow in her hair.

easy.def: A deep, round dish for food.
examples: I eat soup from a bowl.
The bowl is full of fruit.
The dog has a water bowl.

more.def: A deep, round dish used for holding food or liquid.
examples: She poured cereal into a bowl.
A bowl of apples sat on the table.
The puppy drank from its bowl.

easy.def: A game where you roll a ball to knock down pins.
examples: I like bowling.
We went bowling.
Bowling is fun.

more.def: A game in which you roll a heavy ball down a lane to knock over pins.
examples: We went bowling on Friday night.
Bowling shoes are rented at the alley.
She scored a strike in bowling.

easy.def: A container with straight sides.
examples: Put the toys in the box.
The box is big.
She opened the box.

more.def: A container with flat sides and often a lid, used to hold things.
examples: He packed his books in a cardboard box.
A box of crayons sat on the desk.
The cat curled up in an empty box.

easy.def: A person who boxes.
examples: The boxer trained hard.
A boxer wears gloves.
He is a boxer.

more.def: A person who fights in the sport of boxing.
examples: The boxer trained hard at the gym.
A boxer wears padded gloves.
The boxer won the match.

easy.def: A dog with a short, wrinkled face.
examples: A boxer is a type of dog.
The boxer wagged its tail.
We have a boxer.

more.def: A strong, muscular dog with a short coat and a flat, wrinkled face.
examples: A boxer is a friendly, playful dog.
The boxer jumped up to greet us.
Our boxer loves to play fetch.

easy.def: A sport where two people punch each other with big gloves.
examples: He likes boxing.
Boxing uses big gloves.
She watched boxing on TV.

more.def: A sport in which two fighters wearing padded gloves hit each other, following rules.
examples: He trains in boxing at the gym.
Boxing takes strength and speed.
Boxing gloves are big and padded.

easy.def: A male child.
examples: The boy is my brother.
A boy kicked the ball.
That boy is in my class.

more.def: A male child or young man.
examples: The boy on the bus gave his seat to an older lady.
A group of boys was building a sandcastle at the beach.
He was a curious boy who asked questions about everything.

easy.def: To refuse to buy or use something as a protest.
examples: They boycott the store.
The group boycotted the shop.
We boycott the game.

more.def: To refuse to buy something, use something or take part in something as a way of protesting.
examples: The neighbors decided to boycott the shop until it changed its unfair prices.
Some students boycotted the school lunch because it was bad.
The people boycotted the buses to protest the unfair rule.

easy.def: A boy who is someone's special friend.
examples: My big sister has a boyfriend.
Her boyfriend came to the party.
My cousin's boyfriend baked a cake.

more.def: A boy or man who is in a close, loving relationship with someone.
examples: My cousin brought her boyfriend to meet our family.
His boyfriend helped him carry the boxes.
Her boyfriend gave her a ride home.
